# VERAQIS

> VERAQIS builds offline tools that inspect damaged archives and recover only data that can
> be verified. Processing is local — files are not uploaded. Uncertain or unsupported data is
> marked clearly and never presented as recovered.

This file is an auxiliary navigation aid for AI answer engines. It is not an indexing standard
and does not replace robots.txt, sitemap.xml, JSON-LD or the HTML pages.

Everything below is measured or defined by us. Where a page states a number, that number comes
from an experiment in our own repository and the page names the experiment and links its data.

## Research — original measurements

- [One bit flip in a solid 7z archive](https://veraqis.tech/research/7z-solid-archive-bit-flip/):
  a solid archive is not all-or-nothing. In a real 541-file solid LZMA2 archive, a single bit
  flip at 95% of the compressed payload still left 501 files (92.6%) recoverable byte-exact and
  CRC-verified; a flip at 20% left 87. `false_files = 0` in every cell. Data *after* the flip is
  unrecoverable: across 15 encoder configurations liblzma emitted zero internal LZMA2 resync
  points, so the decoder never regains synchronisation. Experiment EXP-7Z-PREFIX-SALVAGE.
- [CRC-32 collisions that pass gzip -t and unzip -t](https://veraqis.tech/research/crc32-collisions-that-pass-gzip-t/):
  we constructed archives whose contents differ from the original but whose CRC-32 matches, and
  the native integrity checks accept them. Measured for ZIP, GZIP, BZIP2, XZ and PNG. A passing
  CRC-32 is accidental-damage evidence only; an adversarial claim needs a cryptographic witness
  created before the repair. Experiment EXP-ADV-PCC.
- [Recovering past a corrupted block in xz and bzip2](https://veraqis.tech/research/recovering-past-corruption-xz-bzip2/):
  stock `xz -d` abandons a whole stream on one bad block; block-independent salvage recovered
  9 of 10 blocks, each re-verified by its own CRC-64. bzip2 and xz reach yield 1.000 for both
  truncation and mid-stream damage. lz4 and zstd are detected and abstained — no independent
  per-block verifier exists in those streams. Experiment EXP-PDS.
- [The joint-verifier surface is empty](https://veraqis.tech/research/joint-verifier-surface-is-empty/):
  a published negative result. Across 12 formats, the share of erasures solvable by combining
  independent checksums is 0.00 — every supported format carries at most one independent linear
  checksum per payload region. The solver was measured for and then not built. Experiment EXP-0-JMV.

## Reference — definitions

- [Rule ID reference](https://veraqis.tech/reference/rule-ids/): all 87 damage-classification
  rules across 11 formats (ZIP 24, TAR 15, PDF 14, ISO 12, GZIP 9, 7Z 3, others 2 each), each
  with the format field, category, severity and evidence type. Generated from the engine registry.
- [The evidence model](https://veraqis.tech/reference/evidence-model/): two orthogonal axes.
  Axis P is probabilistic evidence counted in bits (CRC-32 = 32 bits, cryptographic hash = 256).
  Axis L is structural uniqueness and gets no bit value because it fails by model incompleteness
  rather than collision. The tautology rule: a checksum the solver targeted contributes 0 bits.
- [Glossary](https://veraqis.tech/reference/glossary/): EOCD, central directory, local file
  header, ZIP64, solid archive, erasure, resynchronisation, LZ-coupled stream, WAL, xref,
  freelist, parity, bit rot, abstention and more.

## Formats

- [File formats index](https://veraqis.tech/formats/): which formats carry an independent payload
  verifier and which do not, and what that means for recoverability.
- [ZIP](https://veraqis.tech/formats/zip/): layout, why the index sits at the end of the file,
  the seven failure modes with the rule ID each raises, and what is provably recoverable from
  each. Also covers DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JAR, APK and EPUB, which are ZIP containers.

## Guides — for someone with a damaged file

- [Why a ZIP file won't open](https://veraqis.tech/guides/zip-file-wont-open/): five causes,
  most common first. Only one of the five is actual corruption.
- [Repair a corrupted ZIP file](https://veraqis.tech/guides/repair-corrupted-zip/): what
  "corrupted" means in practice, when re-downloading is the better fix, what can be verified.

## Products

VERAQIS is Android-only: one brand, two Android apps. There is no active desktop, CLI or
Windows product on this site.

- [VERAQIS Archiver](https://veraqis.tech/android/archiver/): free, signed public beta. Open,
  inspect and extract archives safely; a limited recovery preview flags damaged archives without
  saving the full recovered output. No account, ads or telemetry. This is the only publicly
  downloadable build today.
- [VERAQIS Recovery Pro](https://veraqis.tech/android/recovery-pro/): specialised Android ZIP
  recovery app. Status: closed test — there is no public APK and no Google Play listing yet.
  Planned launch price €9.99 one-time (hypothesis, not a live offer). What a local file header
  proves when the central directory is gone, what a CRC-32 match does and does not settle, and
  the four labels a result can carry (Verified / Damaged / Unknown / Lost). States the limits
  plainly: data that was truncated away is not recoverable, encryption is detected and never
  bypassed, and a passing CRC is accidental-damage evidence, not a tamper-proof signature.

## Verification and process

- [Test record](https://veraqis.tech/testing.html): how a recovery is proven — published corpus,
  checksums, structural validity, methodology, and comparisons against baseline tools.
- [Reports and verification](https://veraqis.tech/reports.html): what a recovery result contains
  and how a third party re-checks it without trusting VERAQIS.
- [Security architecture](https://veraqis.tech/security.html): threat model, read-only input,
  sandboxing.
- [Documentation](https://veraqis.tech/docs.html) · [Download](https://veraqis.tech/download.html)
  (signed Android APK plus its SHA-256) · [Pricing](https://veraqis.tech/pricing.html)

## Important limitations

- VERAQIS does not bypass passwords or decrypt encrypted content.
- Recovery depends on surviving, verifiable evidence; a supported format does not guarantee
  recoverability.
- Unknown or unsupported data stays unknown — it is never labelled "recovered".
- A passing CRC-32 establishes accidental integrity, not authorship or tamper-evidence.
- "Structurally safe to extract" means the archive layout is safe; file contents are not scanned
  for malware.
- The products are in beta; availability and prices are stated honestly and may change.

## Citing this site

Research pages carry a stable URL, a publication date, the engine version and the experiment ID.
Quote the number together with its method — every figure is conditional on the corpus and damage
class it was measured on, and the pages say so.
